title: Project tracker
summary: Build your first Effect feature: create, find, edit, and archive learning projects.
outcome: A usable local project tracker with validated writes, recoverable forms, and tests against replaceable storage.
prerequisites: React forms, TypeScript unions, and async functions. Start here before the other projects.
model: Project: id, name (1–100 trimmed characters), goal, status (active or archived), createdAt, updatedAt.
Generate identity once per create attempt. Define whether archived names may be reused before adding uniqueness rules.
Follow src/db/schema.ts and src/db/repos/ for persistence conventions; add a versioned Dexie migration for a new table.
boundaries: React form → createProject operation → ProjectRepository → Dexie. Keep validation in the operation and run the Effect at the UI boundary.

title: JavaScript foundations: a predictable task editor
summary: Learn JavaScript by building a small task editor whose drafts, transformations, asynchronous saves, and modules behave predictably.
outcome: A framework-free CRUD core with isolated drafts, deterministic list transformations, controlled asynchronous operations, and an explicit persistence boundary.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with variables, function calls, and running a JavaScript file. Each milestone explains the language mechanism before using it.
model: Task: { id: string, title: string, done: boolean, details: { estimate: number } }. Seed t1 as Read with estimate 0 and t2 as Write with estimate 30.
Treat a saved task and an editable draft as different ownership domains. IDs identify records; object references identify particular in-memory objects.
Use a tiny in-memory repository first. Promise gates control completion order; a fake clock and ID supplier make creation reproducible.
boundaries: Editor command → pure task transformation → repository adapter → saved snapshot. Keep DOM handlers thin and introduce no framework or database until the behavior is demonstrated.

title: TypeScript foundations: model a trustworthy task domain
summary: Build a typed CRUD domain by turning untrusted input into explicit commands, valid states, and narrow repository contracts.
outcome: A small task service whose boundary decoding, state transitions, patch semantics, and repository interfaces prevent common category mistakes.
prerequisites: JavaScript objects, functions, arrays, and promises; complete the JavaScript foundations lab or demonstrate equivalent ownership and async behavior. Start with strict compiler checking enabled.
model: Task: {id:string,title:string,status:'open'|'done',note:string|null,revision:number}. Decode outside values before treating them as domain tasks.
CreateTask supplies title; PatchTask distinguishes absent fields from explicit null. IDs and revisions come from trusted application boundaries.
Result and editor-state unions use literal tags. Repository functions expose the smallest capabilities their callers require.
boundaries: unknown transport value → decoder → domain command → operation → repository contract → response mapper. Type annotations describe checked code; runtime validation protects external data.

outcome: A version-checked Effect CRUD workflow with replaceable services, explicit resource ownership, controlled concurrency, and deterministic failure evidence.
prerequisites: JavaScript promises and ownership plus TypeScript unions and boundary validation. Complete the two language foundations labs first. Record the installed Effect major version before copying any API syntax.
model: Task: {id:string,title:string,revision:number}. Create commands carry a stable operationId; repository fixtures expose call counts, gates, and an event log.

Examples use version-independent Effect<A,E,R> semantics and name v3 APIs where stated. Use explicit /v3 documentation for Effect 3; consult /v4 and installed declarations for Effect 4. Do not mix Context.Tag and Context.Service patterns across versions.
Separate expected failures such as InvalidTitle, NotFound, Conflict, and TransientStorage from defects. A successful result does not by itself establish remote durability or exactly-once execution.
boundaries: Unknown input → validated command → Effect operation requiring services → composed Layer/runtime at the app edge → repository adapter. Resource scopes and cancellation ownership follow actual application lifetimes.

resources.label: Effect v4: runtime and version comparison

milestones.title: Separate a program description from its execution
milestones.brief: Describe creating t1 Read as an Effect and prove that constructing the value does not write. Read its success, expected-error, and service-requirement types before providing dependencies or running it.

milestones.title: Separate recoverable outcomes from broken assumptions
milestones.concept: Expected errors, defects, and Exit inspection
milestones.brief: Model InvalidTitle and StorageUnavailable as expected failures, then inject a deliberate programmer defect. Make the caller preserve useful recovery behavior without presenting a bug as a normal validation message.

milestones.title: Provide capabilities through an explicit composition graph
milestones.brief: Make createTask require TaskRepository and IdGenerator services. Run the same domain operation with a deterministic memory implementation and a storage adapter selected at the application edge.

milestones.title: Release a repository lease on every exit path
milestones.brief: Wrap a simulated database lease around a task import. Count acquire and release events on success, expected failure, and interruption so ownership is visible.

milestones.title: Limit concurrent CRUD work with explicit ownership
milestones.brief: Import six tasks with at most two repository calls active at once. Keep the import owned by a parent operation so canceling the import stops its outstanding child work.

milestones.title: Retry only a safe unit with deterministic evidence
milestones.brief: Build a create workflow whose first two repository attempts fail transiently and third succeeds. Keep one operationId across attempts, bound retries, and verify timing through the installed version's test clock.

milestones.title: Place changing computations inside the suspended work
milestones.brief: Compare constructing an Effect from nextId() with constructing one that calls nextId only when run. Explain why the two descriptions consume IDs at different times.

milestones.title: Compose operations before running the runtime
milestones.brief: Create a rename workflow that reads t1, validates Study, writes the update, and returns the saved task. Keep the whole workflow as one Effect until the UI or command-line boundary.

milestones.title: Translate rejected promises at the repository boundary
milestones.brief: Adapt a promise-based save API into the service's Effect contract. Map a simulated quota rejection to StorageUnavailable while preserving enough cause information for diagnosis.

milestones.title: Recover only when the replacement result is honest
milestones.brief: Implement getTask where NotFound becomes an explicit missing result for the editor, while StorageUnavailable remains a failure. Do not turn every failed read into an empty task.

milestones.title: Share one service instance for one application lifetime
milestones.concept: Layer construction, sharing, and runtime ownership
milestones.brief: Use a memory repository whose constructor increments a counter. Ensure create followed by list sees the same store within one application runtime, while a fresh test runtime starts clean.

milestones.title: Review dependency provision without hiding requirements
milestones.brief: Ask an agent to add an audit service to renameTask, then verify that the new requirement appears at the composition root instead of being satisfied by a hidden global.

milestones.title: Keep a live resource inside the lifetime that owns it
milestones.brief: Build a repository session with an isOpen flag. Demonstrate why returning the session from an already closed local scope leaves the caller holding an unusable capability.

milestones.title: Observe finalization before treating cancellation as complete
milestones.brief: Cancel a gated import after its lease is acquired. Keep release itself gated so you can distinguish requesting interruption from observing a fully cleaned-up operation.

milestones.title: Propagate cancellation to the external operation
milestones.brief: Adapt a gated fetch-like request that records whether its AbortSignal is triggered. Cancel the owning Effect and determine whether the underlying request actually stops.

milestones.title: Race reads without confusing cancellation with rollback
milestones.brief: Race a primary and replica read for t1 using controlled gates. Decide whether the application wants the first success or simply the first completion, and make the chosen policy explicit.

milestones.title: Reconcile a committed write whose response was lost
milestones.brief: Simulate a repository that commits op7 and then returns a transient error before delivering the response. Retry using the same operationId and prove that the service returns the original task.

milestones.title: Deliver a controlled failure walkthrough for the whole runtime
milestones.brief: Demonstrate one create operation through validation, service provision, resource acquisition, transient failure, retry, success, and cleanup. Include a separate cancellation run with no unsupported persistence claims.

title: Relational foundations lab
summary: Build an equipment-loan database and learn data modeling, constraints, query semantics, concurrency, and safe schema evolution.
outcome: An Effect-backed loan service whose invariants hold under direct SQL, concurrent requests, pagination, and migrations.
prerequisites: TypeScript objects, basic CRUD routes, and a disposable PostgreSQL database. Use the repository's installed Effect conventions.
model: Member M1 Ada and M2 Bo; equipment E1 Camera and E2 Tripod; loans connect members and equipment.
Loan: id, memberId, equipmentId, borrowedAt, returnedAt nullable, version; category names belong to category records.
Use UTC instants and stable generated identities. A current loan has returnedAt = NULL.
boundaries: HTTP decoder → Effect loan operation → LoanRepository → PostgreSQL transaction. Expected failures cross the repository boundary explicitly; SQL and connection ownership stay in adapters.

milestones.title: Model identities and relationships
milestones.brief: Replace a spreadsheet of equipment loans with related tables that preserve identity when editable names change.

milestones.title: Make invariants survive every writer
milestones.concept: NOT NULL · CHECK · UNIQUE · foreign keys
milestones.brief: Enforce valid loan relationships and positive durations even when a maintenance script bypasses application validation.

milestones.title: Read joins, missing values, and totals
milestones.brief: Build a member summary that includes borrowers with no loans and accurate active-loan counts.

milestones.title: Make a transfer atomic under concurrency
milestones.brief: Transfer a reservation between equipment records without leaving a half-applied result after failure.

milestones.title: Read a plan and paginate by a stable key
milestones.brief: Make the newest-loans list predictable without assuming every index improves every query.

milestones.title: Evolve a live schema in compatible steps
milestones.brief: Introduce a required loan purpose without breaking an older application during deployment.

milestones.title: Represent many-to-many membership
milestones.brief: Allow equipment to carry several tags without storing a comma-separated list in a text column.

milestones.title: Separate current facts from history
milestones.brief: Keep checkout fees stable when an equipment item's current daily rate changes after checkout.

milestones.title: Prevent two current loans for one item
milestones.brief: Enforce at most one active loan per equipment item without blocking future historical loans.

milestones.title: Choose deletion semantics deliberately
milestones.brief: Decide what happens to a borrower who still has loan history before wiring a Delete button.

milestones.title: Make missing values explicit
milestones.brief: Implement active and returned loan filters without confusing NULL with an empty timestamp string.

milestones.title: Stop aggregate fan-out
milestones.brief: Report loan and tag counts without multiplying them when both child relationships are joined.

milestones.title: Detect stale edits with a version
milestones.brief: Prevent two staff members from silently overwriting the same loan note after reading the same version.

milestones.title: Observe a serialization failure
milestones.brief: Protect a two-person closing rota from both people leaving after reading the same availability.

milestones.title: Interpret estimates without worshipping timings
milestones.brief: Compare one lookup on a tiny fixture and a realistically skewed dataset before recommending an index.

milestones.title: Treat cursors as validated query state
milestones.brief: Reject malformed or mismatched cursors instead of returning a subtly incorrect continuation.

milestones.title: Make a backfill resumable
milestones.brief: Repair missing purposes without overwriting newer values or restarting all work after a crash.

milestones.title: Test upgrades against dirty history
milestones.brief: Prove an active-loan uniqueness rule against existing duplicate records before release.

title: HTTP and UI foundations lab
summary: Build a small issue tracker while tracing requests, defining resource contracts, designing accessible forms, and reconciling browser and server state.
outcome: A usable HTTP CRUD interface with explicit error semantics, conflict handling, cache validation, and integration evidence.
prerequisites: Basic React, TypeScript, and an existing Effect service/repository seam. Complete a simple local CRUD slice first.
model: Issue I1: title Printer offline, status open, revision 7; I2: title Replace toner, status closed, revision 2.
Routes: /issues for collection reads and creation; /issues/:id for individual reads and edits.
Browser state includes selected issue, unsaved draft, pending request, and errors; persisted issue state belongs to the server.
boundaries: Browser event → HTTP request decoder → Effect issue operation → repository → explicit response encoder → browser response decoder. Run effects at request boundaries and keep UI interaction state distinct from durable records.

milestones.title: Trace one request through the system
milestones.brief: Create an issue from the browser and account for every transformation between a click and durable confirmation.

milestones.title: Decode both sides of the boundary
milestones.concept: Schema contracts · unknown input · output DTOs
milestones.brief: Define an issue contract that remains reliable when callers bypass the form or the database adds private columns.

milestones.title: Build a recoverable accessible form
milestones.concept: Labels · focus · field errors · submission state
milestones.brief: Create an issue form that remains usable by keyboard and preserves a failed submission.

milestones.title: Separate drafts from server truth
milestones.concept: UI state · server state · cache keys
milestones.brief: Let a user edit an issue while background refresh keeps the server cache current.

milestones.title: Use validators for reads and writes
milestones.brief: Reduce unchanged transfers and prevent stale writes using distinct HTTP conditional request paths.

milestones.title: Prove the route-to-storage contract
milestones.brief: Exercise real request decoding, response mapping, and repository persistence in one bounded test suite.

milestones.title: Choose methods from semantics
milestones.brief: Write a small route contract before implementing generic CRUD handlers.

milestones.title: Make errors actionable without leaking internals
milestones.brief: Give malformed input, a missing issue, and unavailable storage distinct transport outcomes.

milestones.title: Distinguish omitted, null, and empty values
milestones.brief: Implement a description update without accidentally clearing fields that a caller omitted.

milestones.title: Specify timestamp and number representations
milestones.brief: Keep due times and revision numbers consistent between browser controls, JSON, and storage.

milestones.title: Make validation reachable by keyboard
milestones.brief: Connect a server-side title error to its control without repeatedly stealing focus while someone types.

milestones.title: Handle duplicate clicks and uncertain outcomes
milestones.concept: Pending state · request identity · replay semantics
milestones.brief: Prevent duplicate issue creation when the browser loses the response after a committed write.

milestones.title: Ignore stale search responses
milestones.brief: Keep the issue list aligned with the latest search when responses arrive out of order.

milestones.title: Reconcile an optimistic status change
milestones.brief: Close I1 immediately in the UI while preserving later changes if the request fails.

milestones.title: Scope private caches correctly
milestones.brief: Prevent issue data from one signed-in account appearing after switching accounts.

milestones.title: Refresh every affected view after mutation
milestones.brief: Keep a filtered issue list and detail view consistent after closing an issue.

milestones.title: Test failures at distinct lifecycle points
milestones.brief: Differentiate failure before mutation, after commit, and during refresh in the browser's recovery behavior.

milestones.title: Review an agent-generated CRUD slice
milestones.brief: Evaluate a proposed route and form diff against explicit HTTP and interaction invariants.

title: Secure CRUD foundations lab
summary: Build a tenant-scoped document desk and make authentication, authorization, browser boundaries, input handling, and regression evidence explicit.
outcome: A defensive CRUD service that rejects unauthorized object access, protects session-based writes, handles untrusted content safely, and runs with restricted privileges.
prerequisites: A working HTTP CRUD slice, runtime input decoding, and basic database relationships. Use a local disposable fixture and established authentication libraries.
model: Users Ada U1 and Bo U2 belong to tenant A; Cy U3 belongs to tenant B. Ada is editor, Bo is viewer, and Cy is editor.
Document D1 belongs to tenant A and D2 to tenant B; each has title, plain-text body, revision, and attachment metadata.
Sessions map opaque random identifiers to server-validated principals; membership and role are authoritative server facts.
boundaries: Browser → session and CSRF boundary → decoded command → Effect authorization operation → tenant-scoped repository → constrained storage. The caller never supplies trusted principal, role, or tenant membership facts.

milestones.title: Separate identity from permission
milestones.brief: Build a document-edit operation that knows who is calling and independently decides whether that caller may edit.

milestones.title: Protect the browser session boundary
milestones.brief: Implement session-authenticated writes with deliberate cookie and request-origin protections.

milestones.title: Authorize the object, not just the route
milestones.brief: Prevent a valid editor in tenant B from reading or editing a tenant-A document by changing its identifier.

milestones.title: Separate data from executable syntax
milestones.brief: Store and display untrusted document text without letting it become SQL or executable browser markup.

milestones.title: Handle attachments as untrusted objects
milestones.concept: File validation · storage isolation · authorized download
milestones.brief: Add a small PDF attachment flow with explicit size, type, identity, and access controls.

milestones.title: Run the application with only needed authority
milestones.concept: Least privilege · database roles · secret boundaries
milestones.brief: Separate runtime database access from migration authority and prove the runtime account cannot change schema.

milestones.title: Turn permissions into an explicit matrix
milestones.brief: Describe who can list, read, create, edit, and delete before scattering conditional checks through handlers.

milestones.title: Observe changed permissions during a session
milestones.brief: Remove Ada's editor membership while her browser still has an open edit form.

milestones.title: Rotate and revoke session credentials
milestones.brief: Make login, privilege changes, and logout produce observable changes in accepted session credentials.

milestones.title: Distinguish origins, sites, and credentials
milestones.brief: Document the trust boundary between a frontend origin and its API before enabling credentialed requests.

milestones.title: Check relationships on nested resources
milestones.brief: Reject an attachment identifier that does not belong to the authorized document in its URL.

milestones.title: Preserve scope in bulk operations
milestones.brief: Define what happens when a bulk archive request mixes authorized and unauthorized document IDs.

milestones.title: Allowlist query structure separately from values
milestones.concept: SQL identifiers · search semantics · bounded queries
milestones.brief: Support sorting and literal text search without turning user options into SQL fragments.

milestones.title: Choose a safe rich-text contract
milestones.brief: Decide whether document bodies are plain text, structured rich text, or sanitized HTML before enabling formatting.

milestones.title: Bound work before expensive processing
milestones.brief: Reject oversized document bodies and uploads before they consume unbounded memory or CPU.

milestones.title: Keep user names out of storage paths
milestones.concept: Generated keys · path confinement · safe metadata
milestones.brief: Store two attachments with the same display filename without collisions or path interpretation.

milestones.title: Record security decisions without collecting secrets
milestones.brief: Capture denied edits and successful sensitive changes without logging session cookies or full document bodies.

milestones.title: Prove the security boundary after agent changes
milestones.concept: Security regression · negative and positive cases
milestones.brief: Review an agent-generated attachment-and-edit feature against a repeatable local authorization matrix.

title: System design foundations
summary: Design a measured modular task board through requirements, capacity estimates, ownership, jobs, caching, and evidence-backed tradeoffs.
outcome: A local architecture workbook and runnable task-board slices with numeric budgets, failure traces, and defensible component choices.
prerequisites: Basic TypeScript, Effect services, and one working CRUD path. No distributed deployment is required.
model: Task: tenantId, taskId, title, assigneeId, status, version, createdAt, updatedAt.
Requirements record measurement boundaries, workload assumptions, latency and freshness budgets, and exclusions.
Jobs and caches carry workflow or derived state; Tasks and Membership retain authoritative ownership.
boundaries: Browser → Effect application services → module-owned repositories → one transactional database, with a bounded local worker for durable jobs. Justify each additional boundary.

milestones.title: Turn product wishes into measurable promises
milestones.brief: Design a shared task board for 200 teams. Tasks can be created, assigned, completed, and listed. Establish what a successful interaction actually promises before choosing components.

milestones.title: Estimate workload with units
milestones.brief: Estimate the board for 8,000 daily active users before selecting infrastructure. Keep every multiplier and unit visible in a small calculation workbook.

milestones.title: Assign module ownership before splitting services
milestones.brief: Implement Tasks, Membership, and Reporting inside one application. Define who can mutate each record before adding remote boundaries or separate deployments.

milestones.title: Separate saved from finished
milestones.concept: Synchronous paths and durable background jobs
milestones.brief: Task persistence takes 80 ms and PDF generation takes four seconds. Design a responsive save flow with explicit export progress and recoverable intent.

milestones.title: Specify cache correctness before speed
milestones.brief: Cache tenant task lists for 30 seconds only after defining permitted staleness and authorization scope. Begin with measured indexed reads as the baseline.

milestones.title: Choose an architecture from evidence
milestones.concept: Decision records and distinct diagram views
milestones.brief: Compare one application plus database with separate Task, Membership, and Reporting services. Use the 200-team workload and observed limitations to decide.

milestones.title: Allocate the request budget
milestones.brief: Break the board's 300 ms create target into authentication, validation, database work, encoding, and reserve. Use traces to check the planning allocations.

milestones.title: Define degraded behavior before implementing it
milestones.brief: The board must save tasks when preview generation is unavailable for 15 minutes. Define the user's visible state and the recovery promise.

milestones.title: Translate latency into bounded concurrency
milestones.brief: A handler receives 50 requests/s and averages 120 ms in the application. Distinguish active handlers, active queries, and callers waiting for connections.

milestones.title: Account for retained data and amplification
milestones.concept: Retention, indexes, replicas, and recovery copies
milestones.brief: Estimate 100,000 task events/day at 800 bytes/event. Separate live operational storage from historical recovery copies and document retention assumptions.

milestones.title: Put invariants at the transaction boundary
milestones.brief: A team may have at most three active projects. Two requests race when it already has two; design the authoritative rule before building the form.

milestones.title: Separate domain operations from adapters
milestones.brief: Swap a persistent task repository for a memory repository while retaining assignment rules. State exactly which claims the fake can and cannot support.

milestones.title: Calculate backlog recovery capacity
milestones.brief: A worker generates three exports/minute while users submit two/minute. Estimate a 20-minute interruption and verify recovery with a local simulator.

milestones.title: Reject completion by stale workers
milestones.brief: Worker A claims job J for 30 seconds, stalls for 40, and resumes after B reclaims it. Protect the authoritative result from stale completion.

milestones.title: Bound hot-key refreshes
milestones.brief: One hundred simultaneous requests miss the same expired dashboard key. Its query takes 200 ms; protect the database while preserving an honest response contract.

milestones.title: Stop old responses replacing new state
milestones.brief: A task changes from version 12 to 13 while a list refresh is delayed. Make the author's confirmation reliable without promising instant global cache convergence.

milestones.title: Trace a failure through the diagram
milestones.brief: Draw create-task authorization, transaction commit, durable job acceptance, and response. Include the case where the response disappears after commit.

milestones.title: Make agent proposals falsifiable
milestones.brief: An agent proposes sharding, Redis, and a broker for 40 requests/s. Review each component against the board's requirements and actual bottlenecks.

title: Distributed reliability
summary: Reason about replication, partitions, outboxes, retries, queues, observability, and recovery using small deterministic failure labs.
outcome: A local reliability harness with explicit guarantees, bounded failure behavior, and evidence from replay and restore drills.
prerequisites: System design foundations, transactions, Effect service boundaries, and a persistent CRUD operation.
model: Task: tenantId, taskId, version, payload; authoritative writes remain in one transactional store by default.
Operation receipt: scoped key, payload fingerprint, status, result, retention deadline.
Outbox and consumer receipt: eventId, entityId, entityVersion, payloadVersion, attempts, delivery or quarantine state.
Recovery manifest: snapshot time, schema version, included stores, validation procedure, RPO and RTO.
boundaries: Simulate replicas and transport locally first. Keep business state and delivery intent in one transaction; model every external acknowledgment, stale read, retry, and restore boundary explicitly.

milestones.title: Choose consistency per operation
milestones.brief: Build a local primary-and-delayed-copy simulator for a task board. Let writes commit to the primary while the copy applies updates two seconds later.

milestones.title: Commit business state and delivery intent together
milestones.brief: Creating a task must eventually update a search projection. Use one database transaction for the task and its event intent, then tolerate repeated publication.

milestones.title: Give retries one owner and one deadline
milestones.concept: Timeouts, backoff, jitter, and safe retry classification
milestones.brief: A read has a 900 ms caller deadline and a dependency that sometimes stalls. Build a retry policy that improves recovery without exceeding the caller's budget.

milestones.title: Separate transport acknowledgments from business completion
milestones.concept: At-least-once delivery and consumer commit order
milestones.brief: Deliver event E to a local consumer twice, including a crash after its database commit but before its transport acknowledgment.

milestones.title: Measure user outcomes instead of process uptime
milestones.brief: Define a task-save success indicator for a rolling 30-day window. Distinguish rejected user input from failed valid save attempts.

milestones.title: Prove recovery with a restore drill
milestones.brief: Your local board takes hourly backups. Delete its live task data in a disposable fixture, restore into a separate database, and measure what was lost and how long recovery took.

milestones.title: Define behavior during a partition
milestones.brief: Disconnect the task service from its authoritative membership store for 30 seconds. Decide which reads and writes can safely continue.

milestones.title: Prevent lost updates with explicit conflict handling
milestones.brief: Two editors load task version 5. One changes its title and the other changes its status; preserve the chosen semantics when both save.

milestones.title: Bind retries to one logical operation
milestones.concept: Idempotency keys, payload hashes, and retention
milestones.brief: The create-task response is lost after commit. Repeat operation key K with the same payload, then repeat K with a different title.

milestones.title: Recover delivery without skipping intent
milestones.brief: An outbox contains events E1, E2, and E3. E2 is malformed for the current consumer; make progress visible without silently deleting the event.

milestones.title: Reject excess work before memory becomes the queue
milestones.concept: Admission limits and bounded Effect concurrency
milestones.brief: A local service can process 20 requests/s but receives 50/s for ten seconds. Add a finite waiting capacity and a predictable overload response.

milestones.title: Spend the remaining deadline deliberately
milestones.brief: A request has one second end to end. Authentication consumes 200 ms and storage acquisition consumes another 150 ms before a dependency call begins.

milestones.title: Order only the stream that needs it
milestones.brief: Task T has events for versions 4, 5, and 6. Deliver them as 4, 6, 5 and define whether the projection can converge without a global event order.

milestones.title: Recover poison messages without infinite churn
milestones.concept: Bounded attempts, quarantine, and safe replay
milestones.brief: A consumer receives 99 valid events and one unsupported payload version. Ensure that failure remains visible while healthy independent work progresses.

milestones.title: Make one failed request explainable
milestones.brief: A task save commits, its response is lost, and the outbox delivery retries. Build telemetry that can connect these facts without logging task contents.

milestones.title: Alert on actionable budget consumption
milestones.concept: Windowed error rates and low-traffic limits
milestones.brief: A service targets 99.9% successful saves. Compare a short incident with normal low-volume variation and design an alert that prompts useful action.

milestones.title: Restore related state coherently
milestones.brief: Restore tasks, operation receipts, and outbox records from a common recovery point. Investigate what happens when those collections come from different times.

milestones.title: Turn a recovery exercise into a design improvement
milestones.brief: Run a 12-minute simulated database outage followed by queue recovery. Produce a review that separates observed facts, estimates, and untested assumptions.

title: Architecture studio
summary: Design and review a tenant-scaled CRUD app with search, media, regional choices, safe evolution, and evidence-producing coding-agent workflows.
outcome: A reviewable local architecture packet with runnable failure fixtures, staged migrations, scoped guarantees, and reproducible handoff.
prerequisites: System design foundations and distributed reliability; comfortable with Effect services, transactions, and basic CRUD authorization.
model: Tenant-scoped Task and Project records own authoritative state; read projections and search results remain derived.
Attachment: tenantId, attachmentId, objectKey, version, state, expectedSize, checksum policy, expiry.
Tenant routing: authoritative home, migration state, version; region authority changes require an explicit protocol.
Design evidence: requirement, assumption or measurement, fixture, result, limitation, decision, revisit trigger.
boundaries: Begin with one modular application and transactional database. Add local adapters for object storage, search, regions, and agent tools; introduce distributed mechanisms only for a stated requirement or measured limitation.

milestones.title: Design tenant-scoped CRUD from the invariant outward
milestones.concept: Tenant identity, ownership, and modular deployment
milestones.brief: Build a project board for 500 tenants using one application and one database. Each task belongs to exactly one tenant and every access must preserve that boundary.

milestones.title: Separate models without prematurely separating services
milestones.concept: Authoritative writes and derived read models
milestones.brief: Build task edits, dashboard counts, and text search for 100,000 seeded tasks. Measure the database-native baseline before adding a separate search engine.

milestones.title: Coordinate metadata with object storage explicitly
milestones.concept: Upload state machines and cross-store consistency
milestones.brief: Add task attachments with metadata in the database and bytes in a local object-store adapter. A two-megabyte upload may succeed even when metadata finalization fails.

milestones.title: Choose a region strategy from actual requirements
milestones.concept: Latency, failure domains, and write authority
milestones.brief: Compare a single-region board with a home-region-per-tenant design. Users are split across two simulated locations with 20 ms versus 140 ms round-trip latency.

milestones.title: Deploy schema changes in compatible phases
milestones.concept: Expand, migrate, contract, and rollback windows
milestones.brief: Replace task.assigneeName with assigneeId while old and new application versions overlap for 20 minutes. Preserve usable reads and writes throughout the rollout.

milestones.title: Run an evidence-based architecture studio
milestones.concept: Design artifacts, experiments, and agent boundaries
milestones.brief: Prepare a reviewable tenant-board design using the preceding labs. Ask a coding agent to challenge one important assumption and build the smallest local experiment.

milestones.title: Keep one noisy tenant from consuming every slot
milestones.brief: Ten tenants share eight job slots. Tenant A submits 1,000 exports while each other tenant submits one; compare FIFO behavior with a bounded fairness policy.

milestones.title: Introduce a routing boundary only when justified
milestones.concept: Shard keys, hot tenants, and migration safety
milestones.brief: A measured hot tenant contributes 70% of database work. Design a possible tenant move while retaining the shared-database default for everyone else.

milestones.title: Rebuild a projection without losing concurrent changes
milestones.brief: Rebuild dashboard counts while 100 task changes occur. Define a source checkpoint so the rebuilt model neither misses nor double-applies changes.

milestones.title: Treat search results as candidates
milestones.concept: Stale indexes, permission changes, and pagination
milestones.brief: A private task remains in search for five seconds after its access is revoked. Prevent stale index state from exposing its title or contents.

milestones.title: Clean orphaned uploads without racing active work
milestones.concept: Grace periods, ownership checks, and reconciliation
milestones.brief: Pending uploads expire after one hour, but one upload may still be running near the cutoff. Build cleanup that cannot delete a newly finalized attachment.

milestones.title: Make attachment deletion convergent
milestones.brief: A user deletes an attachment while a download link is cached. Define immediate product visibility separately from eventual byte cleanup and link expiry.

milestones.title: Prevent two primaries during recovery
milestones.concept: Fencing, failover decisions, and stale replicas
milestones.brief: Primary A becomes unreachable while standby B is four seconds behind. Design a failover drill that does not assume A has stopped accepting writes.

milestones.title: Design conflict behavior before multi-writer writes
milestones.brief: Two disconnected regions edit the same task title and reserve the last project slot. Compare fields that can merge with invariants that need coordination.

milestones.title: Bound the operational cost of a backfill
milestones.brief: Backfill 60,000 tasks while foreground edits target 300 ms p95. Compare a giant transaction with 500-row batches and explicit pauses.

milestones.title: Test mixed versions and job payloads
milestones.concept: Rolling deployment contracts and safe rollback
milestones.brief: Deploy worker version 2 while version-1 jobs remain queued and version-1 web instances still create them. Define the compatibility matrix explicitly.

milestones.title: Challenge the strongest architecture claim
milestones.concept: Counterexamples, invariant review, and agent-generated code
milestones.brief: An agent says the board is tenant-safe, exactly-once, and horizontally scalable. Turn those slogans into narrowly stated, testable claims.

milestones.title: Package a design for independent ownership
milestones.brief: Hand the local board and design packet to another engineer or coding agent. Make normal operation, failure recovery, and future decisions understandable without private context.
